legacy_note: DERIVED, ounce-weighted across the decks the issuer discloses per pit. At A$2,200/oz: Enterprise 115 + Hornet 121 + Orion North 757 + Orion South 1,702 = 2,695 koz. At A$2,600/oz: KGP 1,572 + S2 182 + Sheldon 52 + Taurus 14 + Tobias 79 + Deep South 50 + Comanche 47 + Aries 48 + Drifter 17 + Highway 70 + Heap Leach Pad stockpile 50 + Orion Underground 365 = 2,546 koz. The two sum to 5,241 koz, footing exactly to the group Ore Reserve, and (2,695 x 2,200 + 2,546 x 2,600) / 5,241 = A$2,394/oz. THE PREVIOUS NOTE WAS FACTUALLY WRONG: it said 'Per-pit ounce split not disclosed, so the A$2,200-2,600 midpoint is retained', but the split IS disclosed, in the same document already cited — pages 15-16 carry a full per-deposit Ore Reserve table for all fifteen deposits and the price notes name which pits sit at which deck. So the value stops being a CONSTRUCTED MIDPOINT, which DERIVE OR FAIL forbids, and becomes a DERIVED ounce-weighted average, which it permits. The number moves 0.25%; the provenance is the point. Two secondary findings: the previous note listed only four pits at A$2,600 where the statement names nine, and the document is internally inconsistent by 115 koz (the narrative says the A$2,200 pits hold '2.58Moz' but the four pits it names foot to 2,695 koz, which is exactly 2,580 plus Enterprise). Per the table-wins rule, 2,695 is used. The full spread of defensible readings is A$2,391-2,403.

legacy_note: REPLACES A$1,210m WITH THE AUDITED COMMITMENTS NOTE, and the direction is favourable so the reasoning has to hold on provenance alone. The field is defined as CONTRACTED, non-deferrable spend. Note 19(a)(ii) of the audited FY26 financial report gives exactly that: capital projects and joint arrangement commitments of A$146.411m within one year plus A$75.525m between one and five years, A$221.936m total. The whole A$221.936m is charged inside the two-year window even though part of it runs past FY28 — apportioning it is forbidden and over-charging is the safe direction, so horizon_years is 2.0. The A$1,210m it replaces was a sum of four BOARD-APPROVED project totals (Northparkes E22 A$545m, Cowal A$430m, Ernest Henry Bert A$160m, Northparkes CPF A$75m) assembled by hand across two statements ten months apart, and this record had ALREADY withdrawn the claim that they were contracted — the June quarterly showed the E22 mining contract still out to tender. Board approval is not a contract, the audited note is, and CYL is recorded on this identical basis (Note 17, capital contracted but not provided for). THE MATERIAL CONSEQUENCE: EVN now survives Gate 2 on cash alone rather than only by drawing its revolver, which retires the standing note that gate2.count_undrawn_facilities decides this name. The A$1,210m of board-approved project capital does not disappear — it is the execution-capital input for the §12.2 item 6 denominator migration, where it is admissible as an UPPER_BOUND.

ANNUAL LEG: A$325m, the FY27 Telfer growth guidance. The A$1,065m Havieron leg is excluded — a finite build to first gold that already extends past the window by roughly A$200m. Consumed by §3.2's continuation probe.

legacy_note: Zero SOLD production, which is all P1 counts. The book is 150,000 oz of BOUGHT put options, which per §6.2 earn no credit and score the same as no position at all — options can only ever reduce purity, never raise it above unhedged. VERIFIED THREE WAYS after the previous note was found to contain a currency error. (1) Bought rather than sold: the issuer's own 'full upside exposure to the gold price, while achieving downside price protection' is only possible with a bought put; the A$500m facilities were executed with 'no mandatory hedging requirement'; and decisively the PREMIUM IS A CASH OUTFLOW, since the March quarterly's cash-waterfall note reads 'Corporate and finance includes corporate overheads, finance costs / interest, and premiums paid for gold put options' and that bar is negative — a forward sale carries no premium. (2) CURRENCY CORRECTED: the strikes are AUD, not USD as previously recorded. The table header reads 'Weighted Average Strike Price (A$/oz)'. Sanity check: FY26 realised gold was A$6,223/oz, so an A$4,200 strike is deep out of the money — cheap insurance, exactly as described; US$4,200 would be about A$6,400, near the money, contradicting 'partial downside protection'. (3) The CY26 puts have NOT all expired: 75,000 oz at A$4,200 remain across the Sep-26 and Dec-26 tranches. The book has SHRUNK rather than rolled, from 187,502 oz at A$4,560 on 31 March to 150,000 oz at A$4,650 on 30 June, as the 37,502 oz June tranche expired unexercised and worthless against a realised A$6,468/oz. The CY27 tranches at A$5,000 and A$5,200 were already in place, nothing new was written, and the programme runs off after 30 June 2027 with no extension announced.

legacy_note: ONE ASSET, and this is the classification most sensitive to §8.1's asset rule, so the reasoning is recorded in full rather than the number alone. Table 1 of the March 2026 Group Ore Reserve splits 5.0 Moz into Telfer 1.8 (West Dome open pit 1.4 + Main Dome underground 0.2 + stockpiles 0.3 + dump leach 0.0) and Havieron 3.3. On DEPOSIT names the largest share is 3.3/5.0 = 66%, which would not flag. But §8.1's unit is one processing plant and the deposits the mine plan feeds it, and Havieron has no processing route of its own: it sits 45 km east of Telfer and its ore is treated through the Telfer plant — the same two 10 Mtpa trains that treat West Dome and Main Dome. The issuer's own language is singular: 'the Telfer-Havieron gold-copper complex', 'a substantial and long-life gold-copper operation'. One tailings system, one FIFO camp, one power station, one road from Port Hedland, one Paterson Province approvals envelope. There is no second place to send the ore, so 100%. GGP weights at roughly 7% against the 10% cap, so this moves no weight today; it is recorded because the definition rather than the arithmetic decides it, and a future weight above 10% would make it binding. SITE-LEVEL SPLIT: this statement gives the reserve split above but not the resource split by site. It does record Telfer residual (non-reserve) resources of 3.5 Moz open pit (Indicated 0.4, Inferred 3.2) and 2.6 Moz underground across MDU/WDU/VSC (Indicated 1.8, Inferred 0.8); the Havieron MRE is unchanged since December 2023.

legacy_note: SUPERSEDED BY FY27 GUIDANCE, 20 Aug 2026, and the analyst-assembled sum is retired. The issuer now publishes ONE consolidated line for the KCGM build scope: 'KCGM Mill Expansion and Readiness A$350-470M', so the value is the midpoint A$410m of an ISSUER-PUBLISHED range and the range is recorded for the §3.2 sweep. It replaces A$385m, which was three items summed by hand off the superseded March quarterly (mill tail ~A$160m + tailings A$100-120m + thermal power A$115m) — the VAU precedent applies: where the issuer publishes a consolidated figure, take it rather than reconstruct one. EXCLUDED, unchanged: Operational Growth Capital A$1,150-1,300m as deferrable, and the Hemi Project A$200-250m, which the guidance describes as 'primarily for ongoing engineering and design' with FID still ahead — pre-FID spend is deferrable on the RRL/McPhillamys precedent. COMPOSITION CAVEAT, recorded rather than resolved: it is not stated whether the tailings dam and thermal power items now sit inside the A$350-470m Mill Expansion and Readiness line or inside Operational Growth Capital, which is excluded. The consolidated figure is larger than the sum it replaces, so the recorded value does not fall, but the scope boundary is the issuer's and not this record's. ALSO DISCLOSED AND WORTH THE FLAG: the Mill Expansion Project total is now A$1.75-1.81B against an initial estimate of A$1.53B, a 15-18% overrun, with only A$150-210m of it left in FY27. The two unquantified upward risks the previous note carried — an uncosted renewable energy item and ~A$10m of FY26 Operational Readiness underspend — are not separately identified in the FY27 guidance and are treated as absorbed into it.

legacy_note: DERIVED: 22,500 oz sold-call leg of zero premium collars / (2 x 190,261 oz FY26 gold sold) = 0.0591. FIRST HEDGE VALUE FOR RMS — absence had been scoring the favourable zero. Per §6.2 only production SOLD or written away counts. ZERO FLAT FORWARDS: the book was closed out in the March 2026 quarter ('FY27 gold forward contracts were closed out and June 2026 Quarter forward contracts were pre-delivered. No further forward contracts are currently being considered') and Q4 gold sales were all spot. What remains is 22,500 oz of FY27 zero premium collars, floor A$4,200/oz and ceiling A$5,906/oz; only the SOLD-CALL leg is counted, exactly as for GMD's 4,500 oz of collars and OBM's 33,128 sold calls. THE 40,000 oz OF FY28 PUT OPTIONS ARE BOUGHT AND ARE EXCLUDED ENTIRELY, earning nothing per §6.2 — the premium test confirms it three ways: 'a premium of A$12.4 million was paid for these put options', the H1 FY26 cash flow carries 'Purchase of derivative financial instruments (12,390)' as an OUTFLOW, and the Rebecca-Roe DFS books it as project spend. Book is stable, not growing: identical disclosure at 31 Dec 2025, 31 Mar and 30 Jun 2026. The ceiling sits only ~2% above the 30 Jun 2026 spot of A$5,792/oz, so this sold call is close to the money rather than a token cap.

legacy_note: CLOSES A GAP THE RECORD WRONGLY CALLED A NON-DISCLOSURE. The previous note read 'not disclosed in available sources'; the deck is disclosed plainly in three separate lodged announcements, and the repo was holding a 35-page tables-only extract with no material-assumptions section and not a single '$' character in it. Ore Reserve Commentary p12: 'A maximum A$3,500/oz gold price has been used to estimate Ore Reserves', with JORC Table 1 Section 4 Revenue factors reading 'All reserves are generated at A$3,500/oz or less'. NO BLENDING REQUIRED — all three components of the 4.2 Moz disclose the SAME revenue factor, so an ounce-weighted average is degenerate: the 2.4 Moz base (rr2025), the maiden 1.6 Moz Never Never/Dalgaranga reserve (nn_pfs_oct25, verbatim identical wording) and the maiden 0.26 Moz Bombora/Roe reserve (rr_dfs_oct25, 'Gold price of A$3,500/oz was used for financial model'). TWO PRICES NOT TO CONFUSE WITH THIS ONE: A$3,250/oz is the cut-off grade and pit-shell generation price at Rebecca-Roe, and A$4,500/oz is the DFS/PFS financial-model base case for NPV — neither is the reserve-constraining revenue factor. 'A maximum ... or less' means A$3,500 is a cap and some deposits are constrained lower, so recording 3,500 is the against-the-name reading: it minimises the Channel 2a spread to spot. Effective 30 June 2025 for all three; FY26 statement due ~Oct 2026.

legacy_note: DERIVED as the midpoint of the ISSUER-PUBLISHED FY27 group growth capital range A$250-270m. Value unchanged; citation upgraded from fool.com.au to the lodged announcement, and every element of the previous note is verbatim confirmed. Composition: Duketon A$235-245m (Rosemont Stage 3 underground plus pre-strip of new open pits) and Tropicana A$15-25m (Regis 30% share of Havana underground pre-production). Regis guides group growth capital annually and the note already establishes it as a stable run-rate rather than a depleting project balance — FY26 guided A$240-255m against A$248.1m actual, FY27 guided A$250-270m. Consumed by §3.2's continuation probe.

Four other outside-AISC capital lines are excluded with reasons: exploration A$25m is deferrable by policy; the A$45m underground mining fleet is expressly NOT committed ('the potential acquisition of mining fleet of approximately $45 million'); deferred stripping A$49m is a mining cost, not a build; and the A$46m open-pit owner-operator fleet transition likewise. No range recorded: A$173m is a single published figure. The '173-364' span this note describes is a choice between two ANALYST conventions, not an issuer-published range, and §3.2 deliberately excludes it — probing it would gate on which convention the analyst was undecided about. ANNUAL LEG: the whole A$173m of FY27 growth capital. The A$96m Sugar Zone portion is a finite build, but it is not separable on the horizon question without phasing the issuer does not disclose, so the whole figure is carried — the more adverse reading. Consumed by §3.2's continuation probe.
